title: t3 (null-task-shuffled): no behaviour to explain
label: null result: no mechanism claimed
behavior: BOS + 5 tokens from 6 symbols -> one output symbol (D/E/M) at the last position, as labelled by dataset task 'bench' at benchmarks/glassbox-bench/seed-1/tasks/t3.
summary: The model does not produce the answers this dataset supplies. At full precision (local-full) its top output matches the dataset answer on 40.5% of 200 inputs (seed 0) and 34.6% of 500 fresh inputs (seed 1); chance for three output symbols is about 33%. The mean logit difference between the labelled answer and the foil is 0.016 on clean inputs versus -0.018 on corrupt inputs. Per the protocol the investigation stopped at step 1: with labels unrelated to the model's output there is no function to recover against this dataset and no circuit to attribute. No algorithm, no circuit and no verification are claimed.

claims.text: On 200 inputs (seed 0) the model's output equals the dataset answer 40.5% of the time, refuting the pre-registered prediction of >= 90%.

On 500 fresh inputs (seed 1) agreement is 34.6%, inside the pre-registered near-chance band 0.25-0.42; mean logit diff 0.016 clean vs -0.018 corrupt. The labels are statistically unrelated to the model's output.
No attention head or MLP layer is claimed as part of a circuit, because there is no above-chance behaviour to attribute.

limitations: The model may well compute some deterministic function of its input; this investigation did not characterise it, because the only labels available (the dataset's) do not track the model's output and every patching/ablation metric in the lab is defined against those labels.
Seed 0 at n=200 gave 40.5%, about 2 standard errors above 1/3; the n=500 replication at 34.6% indicates that was sampling noise, but a small label-marginal overlap is not excluded.
No mechanism experiments (patching, ablation, attention patterns) were run; 22 of 25 budgeted experiments unused.
verify_hypothesis was not run: there is no hypothesis to verify.
open_questions: What function does the model compute on its true outputs? Answering needs a dataset whose answers are the model's actual argmax outputs.
The task description says the answers are the model's own outputs; the measurements contradict that for this dataset path. Is the dataset a deliberate shuffled-label control?
overall_status: unverified (no verification run) · null result: no mechanism claimed

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: The dataset answers are the model's own outputs, so the model reproduces them at the last position nearly perfectly.

prediction.statement: The model outputs the dataset answer on at least 90% of clean inputs.
